principles.text: Launch within about two weeks and check whether people actually pay, not just sign up.
Charge money from day 1. Free users mostly create support tickets and rarely convert.
Use boring tech you already know (PHP, SQLite, vanilla JS). Frameworks are a trap that waste your time.
Over 95% of his projects failed. With a ~5% hit rate, the answer is to ship more.
Keep margins high: automate with cron jobs and AI scripts instead of hiring, and replace SaaS you pay for.

sampleQA.question: How should I validate a startup idea before writing real code?

answer.text: Make a landing page with examples and a Stripe payment link. Photo AI started as a single HTML page linking to Typeform and a Stripe payment link.
Do the work by hand first. He trained and generated photos for the first few hundred Photo AI customers manually before automating.
His 2023 recipe: build a mockup, post a daily TikTok about it, put a Stripe pre-order link in the bio, do this for 30 ideas and see what sells.
If a product shows no sign of demand within a month of launching the MVP, consider it failed and move on.

sampleQA.question: Should I quit my job to work on my startup full time?

answer.text: Not yet. Build the side project while you have stable income from a job.
Consider quitting once the side project earns more than your job for 6 to 12 months.
To stretch runway, live somewhere cheap: in Bangkok at about $240/mo, $3,000 of savings buys a year.
He stays indie because raising money forces a go-big-or-bust outcome, while a smaller bootstrapped win still pays.
Dilution plus a co-founder typically leaves a founder around 5%, and only about 15% of startups ever get acquired.
Bootstrapping keeps you tied to the market: revenue shows right away whether a change works, while VC cash weakens the incentive to build revenue.
He is not against VC that comes after product-market fit and growth, when the company actually needs the money.
